title: Western Digital Falls 4% Despite Its AI Storage Pitch; Seagate Drops 5%, Micron Holds Steady
excerpt: Western Digital is pitching AI storage at a major conference this week, but the market is voting with sell orders instead. Whether today's slide is a buying...
content_html:
David Moadel

Tue, September 15, 2026 at 12:52 PM CDT 6 min read

Quick Read

  • WDC and STX fell 4-5% while Micron held steady, splitting HDD and memory into two distinct AI investment stories in a single session.

  • SanDisk's approved $14B buyback and the flat DRAM ETF signal today's HDD selling is a rotation, not a broad storage reprice.

  • WDC's 139% YTD gain needs fresh hyperscaler orders to hold, not conference keynotes that leave revenue lines and customer commitments untouched.

  • Read More: Avoid these 13 retirement mistakes before they derail your future (sponsor)

Western Digital (NASDAQ:WDC) stock is sliding in Tuesday afternoon trading, even as the company leans harder into its AI storage pitch. Western Digital shares are down 4% to $411.34, a mere stumble for a stock that's still up 139% year to date. The move lines up with broader weakness across the hard disk drive (HDD) group heading into a busy fall conference schedule.

Meanwhile, Seagate Technology Holdings (NASDAQ:STX) stock is falling harder, with STX down 5% to $763.35. Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU) stock is holding steady, trading at $926.38. The split highlights how memory and HDD exposure are getting priced as two different AI stories today rather than a single basket trade.

The fund picture supports that read. The Roundhill Memory ETF (CBOE:DRAM) is little changed at $54.83, supported by heavy DRAM weightings from Samsung, SK Hynix (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is off 0.5% to $757.07, so today's HDD selloff is running much deeper than the broad market.

Company Release Doesn't Move the Needle

Western Digital put out a promotional release ahead of an AI infrastructure conference this week, where an executive from its HDD development group is scheduled to deliver a keynote on storing data generated by AI workloads. The release also promoted a sponsored white paper from research firm IDC, which found that 61% of surveyed organizations saw data growth of 25% or more over the past year tied to AI. It amounts to a speaking slot and a company-funded study, well short of a customer order, a product launch, or a financial result.
